James — thanks for the details, this is helpful. High level reply and a proposed sequencing below. I pulled in Jonas (solutions) and Neha (implementation lead) to surface technical constraints.

Proposed sequencing (short):
1) Non-Prod prep: configure a separate SCIM connector + sandbox Okta tenant (so your Non-Prod teams can validate group mappings without touching Prod).
2) Service-account model: create two service accounts in each Okta tenant — one for SCIM provisioning (write scope) and one for event/webhook delivery (read-only token).
3) Pre-cutover sync: run a dry-run SCIM push to populate users/groups with updates suppressed (we'll produce a delta report).
4) IP allowlist staging: we accept a per-region CSV; we'll stage entries in a non-enforced mode for 48h so your security team can verify traffic flows.
5) Cutover weekend: flip SAML metadata, monitor auth logs, and rollback window of 2 hours if errors exceed threshold.

Action items for OptiHealth before our kickoff:
- Confirm Non-Prod Okta details (tenant URL, admin contact).
- Provide a sample group-to-role mapping table (example attached).
- Confirm preferred cutover weekend and timezone (we recommend Sat 10 PM PT or Sun 2 AM PT).

I'll attach a short implementation checklist and a candidate org-policy table for you to review. If that sequencing looks good we'll lock a kickoff & invite your security engineer.

Best,
Priyom Das

Adding a few technical clarifications from the implementation perspective:

- SCIM group mapping: Redwood's SCIM accepts group entitlements (members list) and we map groups to roles via a simple lookup table in our config. Example: scimGroup: "ops_admins" -> roleId: "platform_admin". I'll attach a sample CSV (org-policy-table.csv) with recommended columns: scim_group, role_id, default_ttl_days.
- Service accounts: avoid long-lived API keys on the SCIM service account. We recommend rotating the SCIM service account token every 30 days and using a short TTL for webhook tokens.
- IP allowlists: we support CIDR ranges per deployment region. If you provide distinct lists for us-east-1 and us-west-2 we'll apply them to the corresponding runtime gateway. We also support a staged enforcement flag so your security team can sign off.

Operational note: when we do the dry-run SCIM push, we will produce a change log that includes a confidence score (users matched exactly, users matched by email, unmatched). That helps limit mistakes at cutover.

--
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

James — quick answers and next steps:

- Non-Prod: dry-run without provisioning rights is fine; we'll do a read-only reconciliation first and then a gated provisioning step once you grant the SCIM write token.
- Token rotation: Redwood can automate SCIM token rotation for supported Okta tenants (we integrate with your secrets manager). We'll propose a rotation cadence (30 days) and create a short runbook so your security team can review. If you prefer to keep rotation on your side that's also supported; we'll accept ephemeral tokens during the active cutover window.
- Scoped access: yes — we isolate service-account permissions by endpoint set; SCIM service accounts are confined to user/group provisioning APIs only and have no billing access. We'll document the precise scopes in the runbook.

Next steps / Owners: 
- OptiHealth: share sandbox Okta URL and a sample group->role CSV (Owner: James, due 2028-03-10).
- Redwood (Neha): draft runbook and enforcement staging plan (due 2028-03-11).
- Redwood (Jonas): prepare dry-run scripts and the delta report template (due 2028-03-12).

I'll set a 30-minute kickoff for Mon 2028-03-13 10:00 AM PT and include your security lead — expect the calendar invite in the next hour.

Thanks,
